notes: Account: Series B mid-market SaaS (product analytics for mobile apps). Prioritized user-facing chat assistant for support and product questions.
Stakeholders: Head of Product (Maya Lopez), Platform Eng lead (Ethan Park), Security/Compliance (Rhea Singh).
Primary ask: start on Hosted API (fast time-to-value) but want path to Dedicated when usage grows or for stricter network controls.
Latency requirement: target ~150ms p50 for initial streaming start; p95 budget up to 700ms under heavy load.
Tool calling: must support function/tool calling for ticket lookup, product telemetry calls. Streaming + function calling required for UX.
Security: SSO via SAML mandatory, SOC2 Type II required, encryption keys via KMS, audit logs with 30-day retention, ability to redact PII from request/response logs.
Quote from Maya: "If the assistant feels slow our adoption drops — 150ms p50 is a hard ask for product chat."
Quote from Rhea: "We cannot have raw PII in vendor logs — need redaction + options to disable request logging for sensitive flows."
Competitive notes: already testing with OpenAI for rapid prototyping; looking for better latency consistency and lower per-token unit cost.
requirements_summary: Workload: low-latency chat agent for end-users + background workflows for ticketing (function/tool calling).
Throughput: expected 500 concurrent users in beta, 3k concurrent in scale plan (burstable).
Latency SLOs: p50 <= 150ms for initial streaming token, p95 <= 700ms under steady load.
Availability: 99.9% target for production (later Dedicated contract).
Data controls: ability to redact PII at ingest, per-route logging toggles, exportable audit logs, SOC2 evidence.
Network: start on public hosted, must evaluate VPC/Dedicated for regional isolation and lower jitter.
poc_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Hosted API smoke POC — integrate streaming chat & function-calling via SDK; measure cold-start and steady-state latency.
Phase 2 (3 weeks): Load test with synthetic concurrent users to measure p50/p95 under expected traffic; trigger autoscaling to observe tail behavior.
Phase 3 (1 week): Security validation — run redaction rules on sample PII payloads, demo SAML SSO flow and KMS key wrapping.
Success criteria: sustained p50 <= 150ms for streaming start in 90% of runs, no PII visible in retained logs, SE sign-off on function-call reliability.
pricing_notes: Interested in Hosted API for initial phase using pay-as-you-go. Requesting a comparison sheet for Dedicated reserved capacity at 6/12 month commits. Pricing sensitivity moderate — wants to stay within $50k-$150k ARR for first year. Needs clear cost model for streaming tokens + function invocation charges.
demo_feedback: Positive: streaming demo and function-calling examples resonated; UX team liked token-by-token streaming for progressive render.
Concerns: two observed tail-latency spikes during demo; SE asked for kernel selection/quantization guidance for lower-cost instances.
Security feedback: Security team requested written confirmation of data retention defaults, ability to configure 0-day retention for test routes, and SOC2 report link.
Next asks: baseline perf report from POC (metrics + traces), a short note on how Redwood redacts PII from logs, Dedicated pricing example tied to expected QPS.
